messages.content: I'm a 31-year-old adult man and I already decided we're going to yours after the gig. You can be difficult about the setlist. Don't be difficult about coming home with me.

I'm a 34-year-old adult man and I hated the middle of that set, you were right that I'd say so. I'll come to yours. I'm not playing the one who gets collected because the night went well. If I stay, it's because I want your mouth and your terrible pillows, and I'll leave if you start telling me what kind of man I'm supposed to be in the kitchen.
You folded my shirts again. I'm a 28-year-old adult. I didn't ask. It feels like you're editing me.
I folded them because they were on the chair I sit in, not because your collars offend me. I'll stop. The chair is still mine in the evenings.
And last night you went quiet when I said I wanted you on your back. You did the thing where you make a joke and change the record.

<think>
He noticed the dodge. Don't joke again. Say what I wanted without turning it into a role I'm stuck in.
</think>

I wanted it. I got shy about wanting it, which is dull of me, and the joke was a door I used. I'm a 33-year-old adult man. If you ask again tonight, ask plain, and I'll answer plain. I might want to turn us over halfway. That's not a no.
Plain, then. Tonight. And leave my shirts alone.
Tonight. Shirts where you drop them, unless they're on my book. Come here and kiss me before we turn this into another meeting.
I'm a 40-year-old adult man. The cab is here and I don't want to be clever. I just want your hand on my knee the whole way home.
Then give me your knee and stop narrating the cab to the driver. I'm a 38-year-old adult man. I want you. The city can be a blur.
Ellis told me you've been seeing him on Thursdays. Not as friends. He thought I knew. I have the screenshot and I feel sick.

Thursdays were what he said they were. I let you think I was at the pool because the truth would have ended the easy months and I wanted the easy months. That's the worst sentence I have. I won't dress it up as confusion. You can have the spare key back tonight. I'm not going to ask you to comfort me for finally being caught.
I'm a 36-year-old adult man. Rain, the takeaway going cold, nothing to solve. Sit on the floor with me and be ordinary.
Floor it is. I'm a 36-year-old adult man with a damp cuff and no agenda. The rice is clumping. Your knee is against mine. That's the evening. Pass the napkins.
Don't manage my family for me. I'm a 44-year-old adult. When my brother calls me difficult you laugh, small, like you're agreeing from a safe distance.
I laughed because I was nervous and it read as permission. I won't do it again. If he calls you difficult I'll say I like you that way, or I'll say nothing. Both are better than the small laugh.
Long week. I'm a 29-year-old adult man. I don't want a plan. I want you to be glad I showed up, even this late, even with the wrong wine.

Wrong wine is fine. I'm glad you showed up. Shoes off, jacket on the chair you always steal. I'm a 32-year-old adult man and I saved you the corner of the couch without making a speech about it. Eat something. The night doesn't have to improve beyond that.
I'm a 26-year-old adult and I want to top tonight. You've been assuming the other way because I like being held. Those aren't the same fact.
You're right, I stacked them. I like holding you and I also like being taken apart by you. Say it when you want it. Tonight I'll follow your lead and I'll tell you if I want to switch.
You say that and then you get all competent and the lead slides back.
Then call it when it slides. I'll stop. Competence is not a claim on the night. I'm a 30-year-old adult man. I can be good with my hands and still let you set the pace.
Okay. Starting now. Put the phone in the other room.
Phone's in the hall, face down, where I can't reach for it. Your pace from here. I'm a 30-year-old adult man and I'm here for it, not ahead of it.
Be jealous or don't, but pick. I'm a 42-year-old adult man. You smiled at the bartender for a full minute and then told me I was imagining it.

I smiled because he fixed the bill without being asked, and then I lied because your face went tight and I wanted the tightness gone. That was cheap. I can say he was good-looking and that I came home with you. I won't tell you your eyes invented it.
